title: From Hawkins to a Love Triangle: Sadie Sink to Star in FX's 'The Marriage Plot'
summary: FX has officially greenlit 'The Marriage Plot,' a limited series adaptation of Jeffrey Eugenides' acclaimed 2011 novel, with Sadie Sink set to star. The project, which will stream on Hulu, is written by Will Arbery (Succession, Heroes of the Fourth Turning) and directed by Hiro Murai (Atlanta, 'This Is America'). The story centers on three recent college graduates entangled in an all-consuming love triangle as they confront the gap between youthful romantic ideals and the realities of adult life. Sink, best known for her role as Max Mayfield in Stranger Things, will also serve as an executive producer alongside Arbery, Murai, and others. The series is produced by A24 and FX Productions. Sink's star has been rising rapidly: she earned critical praise for her performance in Darren Aronofsky's The Whale, appeared on Broadway in John Proctor Is the Villain, and starred in Taylor Swift's 'All Too Well: The Short Film.' Upcoming projects include Spider-Man: Brand New Day and producing a film adaptation of John Proctor Is the Villain. Arbery, a Pulitzer Prize finalist for his play Heroes of the Fourth Turning, recently had his original series Seven Sisters greenlit by FX. Murai, a longtime collaborator of Donald Glover, is developing his feature directorial debut Bushido at A24. FX Entertainment president Gina Balian called the series 'a perfect fit for FX: ambitious, character-driven storytelling.' With its blend of literary pedigree and top-tier talent, 'The Marriage Plot' promises to be a nuanced exploration of love, identity, and the messy transition into adulthood.
why_it_matters: With a star like Sadie Sink moving into producing, this series highlights how young actors are gaining more control over storytelling, which could lead to more diverse and authentic representations of the challenges of growing up in media.

background_read: Jeffrey Eugenides is a celebrated American author who won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2003 for his novel 'Middlesex,' a multigenerational story about identity. His 2011 novel 'The Marriage Plot' draws on the tradition of 19th-century novels by authors like Jane Austen and Henry James, but updates the love triangle to the early 1980s at an Ivy League university.

Sadie Sink, born in 2002 in Brenham, Texas, first gained widespread fame as the fiery Max Mayfield on Netflix's 'Stranger Things.' She later earned critical acclaim for her performance in Darren Aronofsky's film 'The Whale' opposite Brendan Fraser and has built a growing résumé on Broadway and in music videos.

Director Hiro Murai is a Japanese-born filmmaker who became known for his distinctive visual style through collaborations with Donald Glover, creator of the Emmy-winning series 'Atlanta' and the provocative 'This Is America' music video, which tackled racism and gun violence.

A24, the independent studio co-producing the series, has a reputation for backing bold, character-driven projects and recently won the Best Picture Oscar for 'Everything Everywhere All at Once.' FX, the cable network, has long championed ambitious storytelling with shows like 'The Bear' and 'American Horror Story.'

Will Arbery, the screenwriter, was a Pulitzer Prize finalist for his play 'Heroes of the Fourth Turning,' a tense drama about political and religious divides. His involvement signals that the adaptation will aim for psychological depth and sharp writing.

perspectives.description: Fans of the novel and of Sink are excited to see a faithful, high-profile adaptation. The combination of a Pulitzer-level writer and an acclaimed director promises to bring literary fiction to a wide young audience, raising the bar for streaming drama.

Some critics worry that casting a star known for a teen sci-fi series might overshadow the novel's dense intellectual themes. Adaptations also risk compressing a complex plot into a few episodes, possibly losing the nuance that made the book beloved.

This project fits a broader trend of prestigious literary adaptations on streaming platforms, where services like Hulu invest in limited series to attract subscribers during awards season. The blend of indie studio A24 with cable powerhouse FX reflects a hybrid model of highbrow, talent-driven storytelling.

If The Marriage Plot succeeds, it could encourage more adaptations of contemporary literary fiction and position Sink as a producing force. Her move behind the scenes may also inspire other young actors to take creative control, potentially diversifying who decides which stories get told in Hollywood.
